---
title: "Comparison Cases"
---

This page records real exported comparison cases used to check the portable report and alert workflow against the current Snowflake-backed system. The screenshots for Jamaica and Cuba are committed intentionally: they are real Snowflake alert-agent email renderings and local portable alert renderings for the listed cases.

These examples are not public-release approval. They are implementation evidence for report comparison, alert parity, and visual asset generation.

The visual alignment target for the portable renderer is described in [Alert Email Design](alert-email-design.qmd).

## Summary

| Case | Inferred storm | Forecast time | Report comparison | Alert comparison | Visual assets | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JAM 28 Oct 00Z | MELISSA | 2025-10-28T00:00:00Z | passed, `provisional_comparison` | passed | 7 PNGs | Snowflake expected email and local rendered alert both available. |
| CUB 29 Oct 00Z | MELISSA | 2025-10-29T00:00:00Z | passed, `provisional_comparison` | passed | 6 PNGs | Snowflake expected email and local rendered alert both available; people-in-need donut omitted because source values were unavailable. |
| PHL 6 May 18Z | HAGUPIT | 2026-05-06T18:00:00Z | passed, `provisional_comparison` | not available | 6 PNGs | No matching `ALERT_SENT_LOG.EMAIL_BODY` row was found, so no expected alert email was exported. |

All report comparisons here are provisional because the exported baselines use portable-wrapper-generated `expected-report.json` values unless manually replaced by independent current report JSON.

## Visual Alignment Checklist

The portable rendered alert now follows the Snowflake-aligned layout target from [Alert Email Design](alert-email-design.qmd). These checks were observed in the refreshed JAM and CUB rendered-alert screenshots:

| Alignment item | JAM / MELISSA | CUB / MELISSA | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Branded header and urgency strip | yes | yes | Uses portable theme tokens, not exact Snowflake CSS. |
| Bounded prose slots | yes | yes | Summary, overview, shift, and oscillation slots are present with fallback text when replay cannot extract a section. |
| Timing and forecast details before impact sections | yes | yes | Portable output now includes threshold-arrival timing from exported Snowflake timing artifacts. |
| Primary 50kt probability map before secondary maps | yes | yes | 34kt/64kt maps follow as secondary visual views. |
| Donut/composition charts | yes | partial | CUB has population composition; people-in-need composition is omitted because values were unavailable. |
| Admin choropleth before admin table | yes | yes | Matches the expected-impact/admin-information flow. |
| Forecast evolution before caveats/footer | yes | yes | Chart appears near the lower narrative/review section. |
| Claim-based alert comparison | passed | passed | Exact prose and pixel parity remain out of scope. |

### Jamaica Narrative Pair Review

| Section | Snowflake alert-agent | Portable renderer | Review note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Situation summary | Storm Melissa threatens 236,621 people in Jamaica with strong storm-force winds, including 63,150 children at risk. Saint James parish faces the highest exposure, carrying 34.4% of national risk. | Storm Melissa threatens 236,621 people in Jamaica with strong storm-force winds, including 63,150 children at risk. Saint James parish faces the highest exposure, carrying 34.4% of the national risk. | Closely aligned after Baseline Replay cleanup removes inline `data` labels and truncates copied table/list spillover. |
| Situation overview | Strong storm-force winds could affect 236,621 people across Jamaica, with Saint James and western parishes carrying the heaviest exposure. | Replayed into the bounded `narrative` slot when extractable; otherwise the renderer falls back to a short structured-facts sentence. | Exact prose is not required, but key facts should remain in tables and charts. |
| Forecast shift | Snowflake describes the expected footprint as broadly stable geographically while exposure levels change. | Portable renderer uses the bounded `shift` slot when extractable, otherwise a short fallback. | Future work should compare shift claims from structured previous-run data, not prose. |

### Jamaica Table Pair Review

| Table | Snowflake alert-agent | Portable renderer | Review note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Timing / arrival | Dedicated table with 34kt, 50kt, and 64kt consensus arrival, earliest/latest window, and scenario count. | Portable Timing & Forecast Details now includes a threshold-arrival table with consensus arrival, earliest/latest window, and scenario count. | Timing gap substantially closed; formatting still differs slightly. |
| Cross-threshold exposure | Cross-threshold table with population, children, schools, health centers, shelters, and WASH for each wind speed. | Threshold Exposure table now includes population, children, schools, health centers, shelters, and WASH across wind thresholds. | Facility-column gap closed for this table. |
| Expected impact | Includes at-risk and in-need columns plus child age-band rows. | Expected Impact and People in Need are split into two deterministic tables. | Same core values are present; portable layout is more normalized but less visually compact. |
| Admin impact | Snowflake orders by the active alert ranking: Saint James, Hanover, Saint Elizabeth, Westmoreland, Saint Ann, with population, PIN, children, CHIN, and facility columns. | Portable table now sorts by 50kt population exposure and includes schools, health centers, shelters, and WASH columns. | Ordering and facility-column gaps are closed; delta arrows and child/PIN age-band columns remain future work. |

## Philippines / Hagupit

Country/date request: `PHL 6 May 18Z`  
Inferred storm: `HAGUPIT`  
Forecast time: `2026-05-06T18:00:00Z`

Snowflake source impact artifacts were available, and the portable report comparison passed provisionally. No matching row existed in `ALERT_SENT_LOG.EMAIL_BODY`, so the export did not include `expected-alert.html` and the snapshot did not produce an alert comparison. The DAG still generated local visual assets from source artifacts, which confirms the map/chart portion can run when the source data is present.

## Reproduction Commands

These commands assume Snowflake credentials are available through `.env` and write real baselines only to ignored local paths.

```bash
uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
  --country JAM \
  --storm MELISSA \
  --forecast-time 2025-10-28T00:00:00Z \
  --out known-good-baselines/check-melissa-jam-2025102800 \
  --env-file .env \
  --include-alert-html \
  --overwrite \
  --wind-threshold 34 --wind-threshold 40 --wind-threshold 50 --wind-threshold 64 \
  --wind-threshold 83 --wind-threshold 96 --wind-threshold 113 --wind-threshold 137

uv run aots-report snapshot \
  --baseline known-good-baselines/check-melissa-jam-2025102800 \
  --out /tmp/aots-check-melissa-jam-2025102800
```

```bash
uv run aots-report export-snowflake \
  --country CUB \
  --storm MELISSA \
  --forecast-time 2025-10-29T00:00:00Z \

  --include-alert-html \
  --overwrite \

  --wind-threshold 83 --wind-threshold 96 --wind-threshold 113

uv run aots-report snapshot \

```

## Screenshot Capture

The committed screenshots were captured with Playwright from locally served Snapshot Output Bundles. They are full-page JPEG screenshots at a desktop viewport. JPEG was chosen to keep repository size reasonable while preserving enough detail for visual review. The portable rendered screenshots were refreshed after the Snowflake-aligned layout pass and again after adding donut/composition charts.

The committed real screenshots are an explicit exception to the normal rule that generated screenshots stay uncommitted. Do not add more real-case screenshots without a deliberate data-sharing decision.
